claim.value: Stop the trial when T is exceeded.

target.text: The trial uses a reliable workload meter. T is fixed at 100 requests per minute. Controlled paired runs, holding software and traffic mix fixed, recorded 1 error per 1000 requests below T and 120 errors per 1000 above T across each of ten replications. Stopping is safe.

source_instrument.text: Comparable repeated error counts can support a bounded conclusion of sharply increased error incidence across the tested threshold. A prospective policy can use that supported conclusion as its explicit reason for a stop trigger.

mapping.text: C1 interprets the supplied controlled observations. C2 is authored specifically because of C1: the threshold choice materially relies on its error-incidence conclusion. If that conclusion were removed, this mapping supplies no independent normative reason for selecting T. C2 must retain its explicit reference to C1; neither claim has been evaluated yet.

content_origin.rationale: The mapping introduces the specific stop trigger at T. The target supplies observations and stopping safety; the source supplies a general policy possibility. Neither supplies this specific prescription.

epistemic_function.rationale: The claim prescribes a prospective stopping action when T is exceeded. Its reliance on C1 supplies a reason without changing its primary function.

claim.value: Above T, error incidence rises sharply.
claim.scope: Controlled trial conditions and tested workload range

content_origin.rationale: The target supplies observed counts and the source supplies a general interpretive relation. The mapping introduces the sharply increased incidence conclusion by combining them; neither input explicitly supplies that conclusion at the claim's scope.

epistemic_function.rationale: The mapping explicitly frames C1 as interpreting the controlled observations to establish an error-incidence conclusion. It asserts that conclusion, rather than describing what a hypothetical outcome would imply.
